prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of Reform UK’s 2024 Contract (policy-focused, under 500 words)

Core pledges
- Freeze non-essential immigration; stop small boats via detention/deportation and potential returns to France.
- Eliminate NHS waiting lists while remaining free at point of use.
- Raise the income tax threshold to £20,000; cut energy levies and expand domestic oil/gas.
- Reduce government waste and taxes to support growth.

Immigration
- Freeze non-essential visas; exception for essential skills (mainly healthcare).
- Leave ECHR; create a Department of Immigration; pick up small boats and return to France; offshore processing.
- Detention for illegal arrivals from safe countries; bar asylum/citizenship if entering from a safe country; no legal aid for non-citizens.
- Deport foreign criminals after sentences; revoke citizenship for serious offenders.
- Bar most student dependants; tighten rules on post-study stays; close fake courses.
- Five-year residency and work requirement for benefits; tackle health tourism.
- Employer Immigration Tax: NI at 20% for foreign workers (exempt essential health/care and micro-firms ≤5 staff). Estimated: savings £5–10bn pa; revenue £4bn pa.

Government waste and regulation
- Stop paying interest to banks on QE reserves (claimed saving c. £35bn pa).
- Departmental efficiency target: save £5 in every £100 spent (c. £50bn pa).
- Halve foreign aid (save £6bn); improve HMRC tax collection; remove retained EU law and other regulations.

Economy – personal
- Raise income tax start point to £20,000; higher rate from £70,000.
- Cut fuel duty by 20p/litre; scrap VAT on energy and green levies.
- Stamp Duty: 0% up to £750k; 2% to £1.5m; 4% above.
- Restore VAT-free tourist shopping; IHT: 0% under £2m, 20% above (charity alternative). Cost c. £70bn pa.

Economy – business
- No corporation tax on profits ≤£100k; main rate to 20%, then 15% in year 3.
- Abolish IR35; raise VAT threshold to £150k.
- Abolish business rates for high-street SMEs; 4% online delivery tax for large multinationals; entrepreneurs’ tax to 5%.
- Planning reform; reduce red tape (incl. employment law changes); simplify tax code. Cost c. £18bn pa.

NHS
- Zero basic rate tax for NHS/social care frontline staff for 3 years; end medical training caps; tuition write-offs tied to service.
- Use independent capacity; 20% tax relief on private healthcare/insurance.
- Vouchers for GP/consultant/operation delays; weekend theatres; charge for no-shows; “Pharmacy First” drive; review PFI; inquiry into excess deaths/vaccine harms. Cost c. £17bn pa.

Energy/Net Zero
- Scrap Net Zero targets and renewables subsidies; fast-track North Sea oil/gas and shale test sites.
- Expand nuclear (SMRs) and other technologies. Claimed public sector savings c. £30bn pa.

Policing and justice
- 40,000 additional officers over 5 years; expand stop and search; tougher penalties on violent/knife/drug offences; leadership reforms; reduce non-operational roles. Cost c. £3bn pa.
- Justice: life for violent repeat offenders; budget from £10bn to £12bn; reopen magistrates’ courts; redefine hate crime; build 10,000 prison places; measures on grooming gangs and youth crime. Cost c. £2bn pa.

Education
- Curriculum audit; restrictions on gender-identity policies in schools; parental notification; single-sex facilities.
- 20% tax relief on independent school fees; scrap student loan interest; 45-year repayment; tighter entry and numbers; free speech enforcement; more exclusions capacity; 2-year degrees. Cost c. £5bn pa.

Benefits
- “Make work pay” via higher tax threshold; training/apprenticeship incentives.
- Two-strike rule for job offers; face-to-face assessments (exempt severe cases). Claimed savings c. £15bn pa.

Brexit
- Scrap retained EU law; abandon Windsor Framework; prepare to renegotiate the EU Trade and Cooperation Agreement.

Defence
- Spend 2.5% of GDP by year 3, 3% by year 6; pay review; Armed Forces Justice Bill; dedicated Veterans Department; recruit 30,000; procurement reform; free education for personnel. Cost c. £14bn pa.

Housing
- Fast-track brownfield; prioritise locals/contributors for social housing; restore landlord mortgage interest relief; drop Renters’ Reform Bill; stronger leasehold protections; construction tech. Cost neutral.

Families
- Target 25% transferable marriage allowance (as finances allow); front-load child benefit (ages 1–4); single-sex public facilities; review online harms. Cost c. £8bn pa.

Transport/utilities
- Scrap remaining HS2 (one-off £25bn saving); end ULEZ/LTNs; no ICE bans; accelerate regional transport.
- New ownership model for utilities: 50% public, 50% UK pension funds; cap standing charges; streamline infrastructure funding. Savings c. £5bn pa after year one.

Agriculture and fishing
- Farming budget to £3bn; replace climate-linked subsidies; cut red tape; buy-British targets; fairer supermarket practices. Cost c. £2bn pa.
- Tighten control of UK waters and quotas; expand patrols; ban supertrawlers/pulse fishing; rebuild processing and fleet; sustainability framework. Cost c. £2bn pa.

Pensions/social care
- Royal Commission on social care; curb offshore tax practices in care; pension system review; adopt 2021 Mineworkers Pension recommendations.

Constitutional/governance and other measures
- Leave ECHR; reform Human Rights Act; reform Lords/civil service; restrict postal voting; PR referendum; British Bill of Rights.
- Sovereignty/free speech package; BBC licence fee abolition; national days; anti-corruption unit.

Funding summary
- Claimed savings: ~£150bn pa plus £10bn pa from assumed extra growth = £160bn pa.
- Claimed costs: ~£141bn pa.
